Testimony of the Division of Licensing and Certification
Maine Department of Health and Human Services
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services
In support of LD 764, An Act to Improve the Efliciency of Certain Department ofHealth and
Human Services Licensing Investigations
Sponsor: Representative Meyer Hearing Date, March l3, 2025
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and Members of the Committee on Health and Human
Services. My name is Bill Montejo, I serve as the Director of the Division of Licensing and
Certification in the Maine Department of Health and Human Services. I am here today to testify
in support of LD 764, An Act to Improve the Efliciency of Certain Department of Health and
Human Services Licensing Investigations.
I would like to thank Representative Meyer for sponsoring this bill. The intent of this bill is to
establish clear authority for the commissioner, the commissioner's delegate or the legal counsel for the department to issue a subpoena for records or testimony as part of a licensing investigation
that is consistent to the authority already established in statutes for investigations by Adult Protective Services at 22 M.R.S.A. � 3480, Child Protective Services at 22 M.R.S.A. �4099,
Maine Emergency Medical Services at 32 M.R.S.A. Ch. 2-B � 90-A, and many other licensing
authorities at l0 M.R.S.A. � 8003-A.
Passage of the bill will allow the department to obtain records and testimony from parties that are relevant to an investigation, including medical records. This will result in a more thorough and timely investigation that affords some level of protection to those parties providing the material in response to the subpoena.
Thank you and I would be happy to address any questions you have.

Testimony ofRepresentative Michele Meyer presenting
LD 764, An Act to Improve the Efficiency of Certain Department of
Health and Human Services Licensing Investigations
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services

Senator Ingwersen, and fellow members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services. I am glad to present LD 764, An Act to Improve the Efliciency of Certain Department ofHealth and Human Services Licensing Investigations.

I submitted this bill on behalf of the Department because it seeks to strengthen the Division of Licensing and Certification's efforts to complete investigations of abuse, neglect, and exploitation of vulnerable adults in a timely fashion.

Currently, DLC is not able to obtain records related to licensure violation investigations from
agencies and entities that do not have current licensure from DLC. This bill would change that by
granting the Department the ability to issue a subpoena to obtain records and testimony relevant to an investigation. This change would be consistent with authority already established in accordance with the Adult Protective Services Act and with other professional licensure boards.

It is absolutely crucial that we do everything in our power to protect Maine's most vulnerable populations, and this bill is one simple way to do that.

The Department will follow my testimony to further explain this proposal and to take any

questions you may have.
